title: Average the quantities too
hook: €3/kg and €6/kg: is 2kg plus 1kg cheaper on average than 1kg of each?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compute a quantity-weighted average rather than averaging unit prices blindly.

misconception: A mixture’s average unit price is always the simple mean of its labels.
objective: Compute a quantity-weighted average rather than averaging unit prices blindly.

claims.text: Material A costs €3/kg and B €6/kg. Compare 1kg of each with 2kg A plus 1kg B. Scaled model; fictional prices; additive masses; no mixing guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Cheaper mass=2kg, A=4.5€/kg and B=4€/kg. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=4.5; B=["/",["+",["*",3,"x"],6],["+","x",1]]; x denotes Cheap-mass. At x=2, A=4.5, B=4. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Total price divided by total mass weights each unit price by its quantity. The simple mean of €3 and €6 only describes equal masses. A larger share of the cheaper material shifts the weighted mean downward.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Fictional material A is €2/kg and B is €8/kg. You combine 3kg of A with 1kg of B. What is the average price per kilogram? Correct: €3.50. Total price ÷ total mass: (€6 + €8) ÷ 4kg = €3.50. The simple mean (€5) only holds for equal masses.
